The district is located entirely within the city of Taguig. It has been represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] since 2007.{{cite web|url=http://www.congress.gov.ph/legislators/?v=province |title=Roster of Philippine legislators |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 10, 2021}} The district was created in 2004 following a plebiscite to ratify Republic Act No. 8487 or the 1998 Taguig City Charter.{{cite web|url=https://lawyerly.ph/laws/view/l1201 |title=Republic Act No. 8487 |publisher=Lawyerly |accessdate=February 10, 2021}} It consists of the western Taguig [[barangay]]s of [[Embo, Taguig|Cembo]], Central Bicutan, [[Central Signal Village]], [[Embo, Taguig|East Rembo]], [[Fort Bonifacio (barangay)|Fort Bonifacio]], Katuparan, [[Maharlika Village]], North Daang Hari, North Signal Village, [[Pinagsama]], [[Embo, Taguig|Pitogo]], [[Post Proper Northside]], [[Post Proper Southside]], [[Embo, Taguig|South Cembo]], South Daang Hari, [[South Signal Village]], Tanyag, [[Upper Bicutan]], [[Western Bicutan]], and [[Embo, Taguig|West Rembo]].{{cite news|url=https://www.rappler.com/philippines/elections/comelec-allows-embo-residents-taguig-vote-congressman-2025/|title=Comelec allows EMBO residents in Taguig to vote for congressman in 2025|date=September 27, 2024|accessdate=September 28, 2024|work=Rappler|first=Dwight|last=de Leon}} The district is currently represented in the [[20th Congress of the Philippines|20th Congress]] by Jorge Daniel Bocobo of the [[Nacionalista Party]] (NP).{{cite web|url=https://www.congress.gov.ph/members/ |title=House Members |publisher=[[House of Representatives of the Philippines]] |accessdate=February 1, 2022}}{{Cite news |last=Sampang |first=Dianne |date=September 23, 2024 |title=Comelec adopts Taguig ordinance on Embo
